facts.text: Onset began as a Spiritualist camp in the late 1870s, drawing Boston-area seekers for annual meetings and a seaside retreat.
A rail line from Boston reached Onset in the 1880s, turning the village into a bustling resort known as the “Spiritualists’ Summer Home by the Sea.”.
The Wigwam, a structure modeled after Native American dwellings, stands as a symbolic nod to Wampanoag spiritual traditions in Onset.
Onset Bay’s river system mixes freshwater and tidal saltwater, creating an estuary that supports diverse aquatic habitats along the coast.
The Onset Bay Association offers a complimentary historic tour map, guiding visitors through the village’s preserved architecture and seaside history.
By the 1920s, scandals over fraudulent mediums and the arrival of non-Spiritualist tourists shifted Onset toward a more secular seaside community.
